claim: In GameNetworkingSockets v1.6.1, packets arriving on a shared direct-UDP listen socket are dispatched by source address: an accepted connection is registered under its remote address (CSharedSocket::AddRemoteHost) and receives only packets from that address; any other source goes to the listen socket's unknown-address handler (challenge / connect / close messages). Together with F-GNS-001, data on an established GNS connection comes only from the address that answered the stateless challenge.
evidence: CSharedSocket::DefaultCallbackRecvPacket looks up info.m_adrFrom in m_mapRemoteHosts and calls that remote host's callback, else m_callbackUnknownAddress; AddRemoteHost inserts adrRemote -> callback and refuses a duplicate address.

sources.location: CSharedSocket::DefaultCallbackRecvPacket (about line 3582) and CSharedSocket::AddRemoteHost (about line 3639) at tag v1.6.1

verification_method: Read-only reading of the shallow clone of tag v1.6.1 used for F-GNS-001; nothing built or run from it.
limitations: Server (listen-socket) side of the direct-UDP path only; the client side of ConnectByIPAddress was not traced. Address-bound dispatch is not identity: a spoofed packet from a connected peer's address reaches that connection (GNS's own per-connection crypto and our DTLS still apply). Relays and P2P signalling are not used by this project and were not examined.
next_experiment: Predeclared A/B (EXP-027): skip our DTLS cookie exchange on GNS only, keep identity authentication; negative tests for unauthorized peers and for the UDP path keeping its cookie.
